newsitem.title: USA: U.S. health officials outline cell, tissue rules.
newsitem.headline: U.S. health officials outline cell, tissue rules.

text.p: U.S. health officials Friday proposed a new framework for regulating medical products made from human cells or human tissues to safeguard against contamination, infection or other dangers.
The system, proposed by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), would set up different "tiers" of regulation according to the degree of risk involved.
Some tissue -- like that taken from a person and transplanted back into the same patient during a surgical procedure -- would face little regulation.
The new system would not apply to blood banks, or organs used in donation, which already have safety standards and rules about screening for such diseases as AIDS and hepatitis.
Tissue is used in skin replacement for burn victims and to repair injured tendons, ligaments, heart valves and corneas. Fertility treatments also use semen or implanted eggs.
As scientists expand their ability to manipulate cells, other treatments are being explored for diseases including AIDS, Parkinson's and diabetes.

The FDA said the goals were to protect against accidental use of contaminated tissue that could transmit disease, to guard against improper handling that could damage or contaminate the tissue, and to ensure that the product is proven to be safe and effective.
All facilities that process tissue would have to register with the FDA.

The agency, which released the proposal on FDA Commissioner David Kessler's final day in office, would not regulate cells or tissues that are removed and transplanted back into that patient in a single surgical procedure.
For tissue that is minimally processed and then used for its normal function, FDA oversight would be limited to proper handling and infection safeguards.

Regulation would be more complex when tissues or cells were processed to alter their biological characteristics or when they were used to perform functions other than their normal ones. Gene therapy would fall into this category.
